title: Grammar: Formal Modal Passives and Semi-Modals in Legal Language
grammarTip:
Пассивные конструкции в правовом и академическом письме:

MODAL PASSIVE для официальных требований:
"must be done" · "shall be submitted" · "may be extended"
"should be considered" · "can be requested"

"Applications must be submitted before the deadline."
"The contract shall be governed by the laws of Kazakhstan."
"Evidence may be presented in writing."

АКАДЕМИЧЕСКИЙ ПАССИВ для объективности:
"It was found that..." · "It has been suggested that..."
"The results were analysed using..." · "Data were collected from..."

💡 Пассив скрывает деятеля → академический/правовой текст звучит объективно
Актив раскрывает деятеля → личная или аргументированная речь

grammarTable.subject: Modal + passive
grammarTable.example: "The decision must be communicated in writing." / "The evidence may be submitted digitally."

grammarTable.subject: Shall + passive (legal)
grammarTable.example: "All parties shall be notified of the hearing." / "The sentence shall be recorded."

grammarTable.subject: Be entitled to
grammarTable.example: "All defendants are entitled to a fair trial." / "Citizens are entitled to legal aid."

grammarTable.subject: Be required to
grammarTable.example: "Employers are required to provide written contracts." / "Companies are required to report financial irregularities."

grammarTable.subject: Be prohibited from
grammarTable.example: "Police are prohibited from entering without a warrant." / "Jurors are prohibited from discussing the case."

grammarTable.subject: Be obliged / bound to
grammarTable.example: "States are obliged to provide legal aid." / "Witnesses are bound to tell the truth."

grammarExtra.title: Modal Passive Patterns in Legal Writing

rows.form: must + be + pp = mandatory (obligation passive)
rows.example: "Suspects must be informed of their rights before questioning." / "The verdict must be delivered publicly."

rows.form: may + be + pp = permitted (permission passive)
rows.example: "Evidence may be challenged in cross-examination." / "The sentence may be appealed within 30 days."

rows.form: may not + be + pp = prohibited (prohibition passive)
rows.example: "Juvenile offenders may not be named in press reports." / "Confessions may not be obtained under duress."

rows.form: shall + be + pp = mandatory (formal written law)
rows.example: "All decisions shall be made available to the public." (statutory language)

grammarExtra.title: Be Entitled To: Rights and Entitlements

rows.form: be entitled to + noun
rows.example: "All workers are entitled to a minimum wage." / "Citizens are entitled to social security benefits."

rows.form: be entitled to + infinitive
rows.example: "Defendants are entitled to remain silent." / "Employees are entitled to appeal disciplinary decisions."

rows.form: Not be entitled to + noun/infinitive
rows.example: "Non-residents may not be entitled to free legal aid." / "She was not entitled to vote at that time."

rows.form: Note: "entitlement" is the noun form
rows.example: "Legal entitlement to a fair trial is enshrined in international human rights law."

grammarExtra.title: Be Prohibited From vs Must Not

rows.form: Be prohibited from + gerund = formal written prohibition
rows.example: "Police are prohibited from searching property without a warrant."

rows.form: Must not + infinitive = strong prohibition (less formal)
rows.example: "Police must not search property without a warrant." (same meaning, less formal register)

rows.form: Be banned from + gerund = informal equivalent
rows.example: "He was banned from practising law." (disciplinary, informal register)

rows.form: "Be prohibited from" is most appropriate in legal documents
rows.example: "The organisation is prohibited from engaging in political campaigning."

grammarExtra.title: Be Required To vs Have To: Formality Register

rows.form: Be required to + infinitive = formal external obligation
rows.example: "All companies are required to file annual tax returns." (legal requirement)

rows.form: Have to + infinitive = similar meaning, less formal
rows.example: "All companies have to file annual tax returns." (same meaning, more conversational)

rows.form: Be obliged to + infinitive = duty-based obligation
rows.example: "States are obliged to investigate credible human rights violations." (moral/legal duty)

rows.form: Be bound to + infinitive = legally committed
rows.example: "Parties are bound to comply with the terms of the contract."

grammarExtra.title: Negative Permissions and Prohibitions in Legal Texts

rows.form: Not be entitled to = lack of right
rows.example: "Non-citizens are not entitled to vote in national elections."

rows.form: Not be required to = no obligation
rows.example: "Witnesses are not required to answer self-incriminating questions."

rows.form: Not be permitted to = formal prohibition
rows.example: "Lawyers are not permitted to disclose privileged communications."

rows.form: Be exempt from = official exception from obligation
rows.example: "Diplomatic personnel are exempt from local taxation."

exercises.text: "Suspects ___ ___ of their right to remain silent before police questioning." (inform — obligation)
exercises.hint: "Must be + pp" = obligation passive — suspects are the object

exercises.text: "All defendants ___ ___ legal representation, regardless of their ability to pay."
exercises.hint: "Are entitled to + noun/infinitive" = have the right to
"May not + infinitive" = formal prohibition (also: are prohibited from entering)

exercises.text: "All lawyers ___ ___ complete 20 hours of professional development training per year."
exercises.hint: "Are required to + infinitive" = formal external obligation

exercises.instruction: Choose the most formal legal prohibition.
exercises.text: "Jurors ___ ___ discussing the case with members of the public during the trial."
exercises.hint: "Are prohibited from + gerund" = most formal written prohibition

exercises.text: "All court decisions ___ ___ recorded and made available to the public." (legal document)
exercises.hint: "Shall be + pp" = mandatory passive in formal written law

exercises.text: "Workers ___ ___ a minimum of 28 days' paid leave per year."
exercises.hint: "Are entitled to + noun" = have the legal right to

exercises.text: "States ___ ___ investigate credible human rights violations reported to them."
exercises.hint: "Are obliged to + infinitive" = have a duty to (moral/legal)

exercises.text: "The sentence ___ ___ within 30 days if new evidence comes to light." (may — allow)
exercises.hint: "May be + pp" = permitted/possible in passive form

exercises.text: "Diplomatic personnel ___ ___ prosecution in the host country under international law."
exercises.hint: "Are exempt from + noun/gerund" = officially excused from

exercises.text: "Witnesses ___ ___ self-incriminating questions — they have the right to refuse." (not obligated)
exercises.hint: "Are not required to + infinitive" = have no obligation to

exercises.text: "Confessions ___ not ___ obtained through coercion or threats." (may — passive prohibition)
exercises.hint: "May not be + pp" = formal passive prohibition

exercises.instruction: Choose the most formal way to express this right.
exercises.text: "You can take the case to a higher court."
opts: You may take the case to a higher court.
You are entitled to appeal the decision to a higher court.
You're allowed to go to a higher court.
exercises.correct: You are entitled to appeal the decision to a higher court.
exercises.hint: "Are entitled to + infinitive" = most formal expression of a right

exercises.text: "All parties ___ ___ notified in writing at least 14 days before the hearing." (shall — passive)
exercises.hint: "Shall be + pp" = mandatory requirement in legal document

exercises.instruction: Which sentence uses "be bound to" correctly?
opts: She is bound to sign the document.
The company is bound to comply with the terms of the agreement.
Judges are bound to follow their personal opinions.
exercises.correct: The company is bound to comply with the terms of the agreement.

exercises.instruction: What is the most appropriate formal legal register?
exercises.text: The police cannot enter your home without a warrant.
opts: "The police can't enter your home without a warrant."
"Police must not enter without a warrant."
"Police officers are prohibited from entering private property without a valid warrant."
"You don't have to let the police in."
exercises.correct: "Police officers are prohibited from entering private property without a valid warrant."
exercises.hint: "Are prohibited from + gerund" = most formal register for a legal text

questions.text: "Suspects ___ ___ of their rights before any police interview." (must — passive)
"All citizens ___ ___ free legal aid if they cannot afford a lawyer." (= have the right to)
questions.hint: "Are entitled to + noun" = have the legal right to

questions.text: "The verdict ___ ___ in open court in front of all parties." (shall — passive obligation in law)
questions.hint: "Shall be + pp" = formal mandatory passive in legal documents

questions.text: "Employers ___ ___ providing written employment contracts within 8 weeks of hiring." (formal prohibition)
questions.correct: are prohibited from / must not be found
questions.hint: "Are prohibited from + gerund" = formal written prohibition

questions.text: "Companies ___ ___ report significant financial irregularities to the regulator." (external legal requirement)
questions.hint: "Are required to + infinitive" = formal external legal obligation

questions.text: "Are prohibited from" and "don't have to" express the same legal meaning.
questions.hint: "Prohibited from" = forbidden; "don't have to" = no obligation (permitted)

questions.text: "States ___ ___ providing legal aid to those who cannot access justice." (duty — obliged)
questions.correct: are obliged to / are required to
questions.hint: "Are obliged to / required to + infinitive" = have a duty to

questions.text: "The decision ___ ___ within 28 days of the original ruling." (may — passive permission)
questions.hint: "May be + pp" = passive permission — the decision can be appealed

questions.text: "Diplomatic personnel ___ ___ local prosecution under the Vienna Convention." (exempt from)
questions.hint: "Are exempt from + noun/gerund" = officially excused from obligation

questions.text: "Witnesses ___ ___ self-incriminating statements — they may exercise the right to silence." (no obligation)
questions.hint: "Are not required to + infinitive" = have no obligation to do this

questions.text: "All court proceedings ___ ___ recorded and archived for public access." (shall — formal law)
questions.hint: "Shall be + pp" = mandatory formal legal requirement

questions.text: Which is the most formal and precise legal prohibition?
opts: "Police must not search without a warrant."
"Police officers are prohibited from conducting searches without a valid judicial warrant."
"The police shouldn't search without a warrant."
questions.correct: "Police officers are prohibited from conducting searches without a valid judicial warrant."
questions.hint: "Are prohibited from + gerund" = most formal legal register
